issue: Blocked task's edit action is fully disabled, so description and priority cannot be changed
actual: On blocked tasks (Complete tax filing, Submit final report, Prepare launch deck) the edit button carries the HTML `disabled` attribute; clicking it times out ("element is not enabled") and no task form opens. A DOM scan of the blocked task card shows only complete (disabled), edit (disabled) and delete (enabled) — there is no inline or alternative control for description or priority. The spec requires description and priority to remain editable while blocked, and only title/deadline to be locked.

evidence: Single prereq at creation ("Prepare launch deck" -> Buy groceries) and two prereqs via edit ("Write launch blog post" -> Review project proposal + Schedule dentist appointment). Saved task shows state=blocked with "2 prerequisites incomplete".

Edited unblocked "Write blog post": title->"Write launch blog post", description->"Announcement article for the launch", deadline->Sep 15, priority->Low, added 2 prerequisites; all retained after save. Delete then removed it from the list (active 7 -> 6).
Completed "Buy groceries": it left the active list, counts changed from "6 active, 2 completed" to "5 active, 3 completed" (Active 6->5, Completed 2->3).

While "Buy groceries" was incomplete, "Prepare launch deck" had complete.enabled=false and state=blocked. After completing "Buy groceries", it flipped to state=active with an enabled complete toggle and a "1 prerequisite completed" indicator.

Active view (toggle selected) lists exactly the 5 active tasks and shows "Active 5"; clicking "Completed 3" switches selection and lists exactly the 3 completed tasks (Buy groceries, Reply to client emails, Organize desk). Summary reads "5 active, 3 completed".
After completing "Buy groceries" it is not deleted: it appears in the completed view with its full data (Low, description, Tomorrow) and retains an enabled toggle-complete (reopen) and delete action.

Cards show title + priority always ("Write blog post | Medium" with no desc/deadline), description and deadline when supplied ("Prepare launch deck | High | Slides for the Q4 product launch | Sep 5"), blocking state ('Prerequisite "Buy groceries" incomplete', "2 prerequisites incomplete"). Completed tasks render with computed text-decoration: line-through and complete.state="completed".

Direct: editing "Buy groceries" omits its dependent "Prepare launch deck" from prerequisite options; editing "Review project proposal" omits dependents "Complete tax filing" and "Submit final report". Indirect: after building chain Complete tax filing -> Review project proposal -> Schedule dentist appointment, editing "Schedule dentist appointment" omits both "Review project proposal" (direct) and "Complete tax filing"/"Submit final report" (indirect). Self is never listed.

Hovering the blocked warning on "Complete tax filing" opens a role=tooltip reading "Dependency Chain | Review project proposal pending | Schedule dentist appointment pending" — the full transitive chain with each pending prerequisite identified.

Dependency connections render as SVG paths with stroke-dasharray "6px, 4px" inside hoverable g.pointer-events-auto.cursor-pointer groups. Hovering a connection flips its data-state closed -> instant-open and shows a role=tooltip "Dependency Chain: Complete tax filing (pending) -> Review project proposal (pending) -> Schedule dentist appointment (pending)"; a different connection yields its own chain ending in Submit final report.

issue: Reopening a prerequisite leaves the dependent task simultaneously completed and blocked, and permanently stuck
actual: Setup: "Prepare launch deck" (prereq: "Buy groceries") was completed while its prerequisite was completed. Reopening "Buy groceries" was neither prevented nor did it reset the dependent. Afterwards "Prepare launch deck" is still state=completed, still listed in the Completed view (counted in "Completed 3"), rendered line-through, yet simultaneously shows the blocked warning 'Prerequisite "Buy groceries" incomplete'. Its complete toggle and edit button are both disabled=true, so the user cannot reopen or edit it to escape the contradictory completed+blocked state.
